# Sunday Public Sail

Free boat rides on Lake Union with volunteer skippers and crew, aboard historic vessels — sprit boats, steamboats, electric boats, schooners, ketches, yawls, and yachts. Part of our [Free Programs](https://www.cwb.org/free-programs).

## 2026 Public Sail Dates

- April 12
- May 10 (Mother's Day)
- June 14 (International Soccer Celebration Public Sail)
- July 26
- August 30
- September 27

## Registration

Registration begins at 1:00pm in front of the Wagner Education Center. Sign-up is first-come, first-served and in person only. Arriving early is recommended.

## How It Works

- Everyone in your party must be present to sign up; each passenger receives a wristband with a call time and boat name.
- Boats generally depart between 1:15pm and 5:00pm. Plan for a 45-minute ride.
- About four to six boats run each month, from 4–6 passengers on the smallest to 17–20 on the largest.
- Each party may choose only one boat ride.
- No line cutting or holding spots for others.
- No reservations by phone or online.
- No age restrictions; life jackets are provided. Boarding involves steps of up to 1.5 feet onto a shifting vessel, and staff cannot assist with lifts.
- Each passenger must sign a digital waiver; parents sign for each child.

## Steamship Sundays

On the last Sunday of each month, passengers can line up for the 3pm Virginia V steamship ride. [https://virginiav.org/](https://virginiav.org/)

## Good to Know

- **Rain or shine:** Rides are postponed only for unsafe weather or wind.
- **Rowboat alternatives:** If rides fill up, [rent a rowboat](https://www.cwb.org/rent) or use the Public Peapod Program (two peapods, one-hour rows, first-come, first-served).
- **Restrooms:** Available at the Wagner Education Center from 12:30pm; nearby businesses before then.
- **Food and drink:** Water bottles are fine; eating and drinking on rides is discouraged. No alcohol.
- **Pets:** No dogs on Public Sail rides; service dogs generally accommodated if staff are notified at sign-up.
- **Cost:** Rides are free, though [donations](https://www.cwb.org/give) are appreciated and fund boat maintenance.
